text: Ahuhɔ̃e fesre gãwo kple gli suewo mate ŋu axe mɔ na amedzidzedze si woɖo le be nenɔ anyi ɣeyiɣi didi aɖeke o.
text_en: Its large glazed windows and thin walls would not have been able to resist a determined attack for long.

text: Le ƒe 1480 wo me esi Lord Haslings dze etutu gɔ me ma, dukɔ la nɔ anyi le ŋutifafa me eye ɖeko wohiã na kpɔtɔxoxlã ɖe adzoha sue siwo nɔ tsatsam la nu.
text_en: In the 1480s, when its construction was begun by Lord Hastings, the country was relatively peaceful and defense was only required against small bands of roving marauders.

text: Ŋusẽ ƒe sɔsɔ ƒe ɖoɖo nye mɔnu aɖe si dzi Europa dukɔwo to hekpɔ egbɔ be ŋusẽ si Europa dukɔwo kpɔ ɖe woawo ŋutɔ woƒe dukɔwo dzi la naganɔ anyi.
text_en: The balance of power was a system in which European nations sought to maintain the national sovereignty of all European states.

text: Ɖoɖo lae nye be ele be Europa dukɔwo katã nakpɔ egbɔ be yewo xe mɔ na dukɔ ɖeka, ale be magakpɔ ŋusẽ akpã o, eya ta dziɖuɖuwo trɔ habɔbɔ siwo me wonɔ kple dukɔ bubuwo edzi edzi, ale be ŋusẽ sɔsɔe nanɔ anyi.
text_en: The concept was that all European nations had to seek to prevent one nation from becoming powerful, and thus national governments often changed their alliances in order to maintain the balance.

text: Spaintɔwo ƒe Fiayeyeɖoɖo Ʋa la nye aʋa gbãtɔ si ƒe kuxi koŋ kuɖe ŋusẽ sɔsɔe ŋu.
text_en: The War of Spanish Succession marked the first war whose central issue was the balance of power.

text: Esia he tɔtrɔ vevi aɖe vɛ, le esime Europa ŋusẽwo magate ŋu awɔ aye be yewo le aʋawɔm ɖe subɔsubɔ ta o. Eya ta Ƒe Blaetɔ̃ ƒe Aʋa la nye aʋa susɔe si woyɔ be subɔsubɔ-ʋa.
text_en: This marked an important change, as European powers would no longer have the pretext of being religious wars. Thus, the Thirty Years' War would be the last war to be labeled a religious war.

text: Herostratus tɔ dzo Artemis ƒe gbedoxɔ le Efeso le Siamlɔm 21, 356 D.M.Ŋ.
text_en: The temple of Artemis at Ephesus was destroyed on July 21, 356 BCE in an act of arson committed by Herostratus.

text: Le ŋutinya la nu la, nu si nye megbeda nɛ lae nye be yeawɔ ŋkɔ, meka nu si adzɔ o. Dzi ku Efesotɔwo alegbegbe, ale be woɖe gbeƒã be womalé Herostratus ƒe ŋkɔ ɖi gbeɖe o.
text_en: According to the story, his motivation was fame at any cost. The Ephesians, outraged, announced that Herostratus' name never be recorded.

text: Emegbe la, Hela ŋutinyaŋlɔla Strabo lé eƒe ŋkɔ ɖi, esia tae míenyae egbe. Wotsrɔ̃ gbedoxɔ la le zã si me ke wodzi Alexander Gã tɔ la.
text_en: The Greek historian Strabo later noted the name, which is how we know today. The temple was destroyed on the same night that Alexander the Great was born.

text: Esi Alexander vazu fia la, edoe ɖa be yeagbugbɔ atu gbedoxɔ la, ke wogbe eƒe biabia la. Emegbe esi Alexander ku vɔ la, wogbugbɔ tu gbedoxɔ la le ƒe 323 D.M.Ŋ.
text_en: Alexander, as king, offered to pay to rebuild the temple, but his offer was denied. Later, after Alexander died, the temple was rebuilt in 323 BCE.

text: Kpɔ egbɔ be wò asi gbɔdzɔ ale si dze le esime ègale gbeɖiɖi nyuitɔwo ƒom- gadze agbagba be yemele asi ʋãm akpa o.
text_en: Make sure your hand is as relaxed as possible while still hitting all the notes correctly - also try not to make much extraneous motion with your fingers.

text: Le mɔ sia dzi la, màna be ɖeɖi nate ŋu wò akpa o. Ɖo ŋku edzi be mehiã be nàzã ŋusẽ geɖe atsɔ aƒo kaawo me ale be wòaɖi sesiẽ abe ale si kasaŋku le ene o.
text_en: This way, you will tire yourself out as little as possible. Remember there's no need to hit the keys with a lot of force for extra volume like on the piano.

text: Le saŋku si wohena zazã me la, nenye be nèdi be gbeɖiɖia nasẽ ɖe edzi la, he ayagbɔnu la me.
text_en: On the accordion, to get extra volume, you use the bellows with more pressure or speed.

text: Vivimekadodo nye didi vevie hena hadede kple, kadodo kple alo nyanya ƒe ame si nɔnɔ kuɖe nyateƒe nu aɖe si nye gãtɔ, mawu aɖe, gbɔgbɔmenyateƒe aɖe, alo Mawu (ŋu).
text_en: Mysticism is the pursuit of communion with, identity with, or conscious awareness of an ultimate reality, divinity, spiritual truth, or God.

text: Xɔsetɔ la dina be yeado ka kple mawu aɖe, alo mawuwo alo aganya nane tso eŋu alo woŋu.
text_en: The believer seeks a direct experience, intuition, or insight into divine reality/the deity or dieties.

text: Ame siwo kplɔ subɔsubɔ sia ɖo la nɔa agbe le mɔ aɖe nu, nuwɔna aɖewo le wosi siwo naa be numetoto siawo vana eme.
text_en: Followers pursue certain ways of living, or practices that are intended to nurture those experiences.

text: Woate ŋu ade vovototo vivimekadodo me tso subɔsubɔ bubuwo gbɔ to gbetete ɖe ale si ame si le subɔsubɔ sia wɔm la nɔna ŋudzɔ tɔxe aɖe me le susu me kuɖe eƒe numetoto ŋu, vevietɔ esi me ŋutifafa, nu detonyanya, yayra alo ŋudzedzekpɔkpɔ gɔ hã nɔna.
text_en: Mysticism can be distinguished from other forms of religious belief and worship by its emphasis on the direct personal experience of a unique state of consciousness, particularly those of a peaceful, insightful, blissful, or even ecstatic character.

text: Sikhism nye subɔsubɔ aɖe tso India ƒe kɔntinent ƒe akpa aɖe. Edze egɔme le Punjab- nyigba la dzi le ƒe alafa 15 me tso hatsotso aɖe si do le Hindu blemakɔnyinyi la me.
text_en: Sikhism is a religion from the Indian sub-continent. It originated in the Punjab region during the 15th century from a sectarian split within the Hindu tradition.

text: Sikhtɔwo kpɔ woƒe xɔse be enye subɔsuhɔ aɖe si to vovo na Hindu subɔsubɔ eye wode dzesii be edo tso Hindu kɔnyinyiwo me.
text_en: Sikhs consider their faith to be a separate religion from Hinduism though they acknowledge its Hindu roots and traditions.

text: Sikhtɔwo yɔna woƒe subɔsubɔha be Gurmat, si nye Punjabigbe na "guru ƒe mɔ". Guru nye India subɔsubɔhawo katã ƒe gɔmeɖokpe, ke le Sikh'-subɔsubɔ me la, vevienyenye si le eŋu la nye Sikkh dzixɔsewo ƒe gɔmeɖokpe.
text_en: Sikhs call their religion Gurmat, which is Punjabi for "way of the guru". The guru is a fundamental aspect of all Indian religions but in Sikhism has taken on an importance that forms the core of Sikh beliefs.

text: Guru Nanak (ƒe 1469-1539) yetu subɔsubɔ la le ƒe alafa 15 lia me. Guru asieke bubuwo vanɔ eteƒe le eƒe anyimanɔmanɔ megbe.
text_en: The religion was founded in the 15th century by Guru Nanak (1469–1539). There followed in succession a further nine gurus.

text: Ke le Masa 1956 me la, wodo Krushchev ƒe ŋugbedodowo kpɔ, le esime zi tɔ ɖe dɔwɔla siwo nɔ tsitre tsim ɖe nuɖuɖuwo ƒe vɔvɔ kple fetu nu tsotsoɖawo ŋu la dome le Poland, eye wɔna sia trɔ zu tsitretsitsi gbadzawo ɖe Dziɖuɖu si me nunɔamesiwo katã nye dukɔ la tɔ ŋu.
text_en: However, in June 1956, Krushchev's promises were put to the test when riots in Poland, where workers were protesting against food shortages and wage cuts, turned into a general protest against Communism.

text: Togbɔ be le nuwuwua la, Krushchev ɖo asrafowo ɖa be woana be nuwo naɖɔ ɖo la, eʋu mɔ na dzizizi aɖewo ƒe emevava eye wòlɔ̃ be yeatia ame nyanyɛ si nye Wladyslaw Gomulka be wòava zu dɔnunɔlawo ƒe tatɔ yeye la.
text_en: Although in the end, Krushchev sent in tanks to restore order, he did give way to some economic demands and agreed to appoint the popular Wladyslaw Gomulka as the new prime minister.

text: Indus Togbe ƒe Ŋkuʋuʋu-gbenɔnɔ nye Gadzĩ Ɣeyiɣi ƒe Ŋkuʋuʋu-gbenɔnɔ si yi edzi le India ƒe dziehe ɣetoɖoƒe-nyigba gã te helɔ egbegbe Pakistan kple nuto bubu siwo le dzieheɣetoɖoƒe India kple dzieheɣedzeƒe Afghanistan la ɖe eme.
text_en: The Indus Valley Civilization was a Bronze Age civilisation in the northwest Indian subcontinent encompassing most of modern-day Pakistan and some regions in northwest India and northeast Afghanistan.

text: Ŋkuʋuʋu-gbenɔnɔ yi edzi nyui le Indus Tɔsia ƒe tsido, si nye afi si wòɖe eƒe ŋkɔ tsoe me.
text_en: The civilisation flourished in the basins of the Indus River wherefore it derives its name.

text: Togbɔ be agbalẽnyala aɖewo bui be ɖe ale si ŋkuʋuʋu-gbenɔnɔ gayi edzi le Sarasvati Tɔsisia me ta la, edze be woayɔe be Indus-Sarasvati Ŋkuʋuʋu-gbenɔnɔ la, ame bubuwo yɔnae be Harappa Ŋkuʋuʋu-gbenɔnɔ, si nye Harappa, teƒe gbãtɔ si tomekulawo ku le ƒe 1920 wo me.
text_en: Although some scholars speculate that since the civilisation also existed in the basins of the now dried up Sarasvati River, it should be aptly called the Indus-Sarasvati Civilization, while some call it the Harappan Civilization after Harappa, the first of its sites to be excavated in the 1920s.

text: Asrafowo ƒe agbɔsɔsɔ le Roma fiaɖuƒe la me na be atikewɔnyawo de ŋgɔ.
text_en: The militaristic nature of the Roman empire aided in the development of medical advances.

text: Fia Augustus xɔ ɖɔkitawo eye wògaɖo Roma Atikewɔsrafowo ƒe Habɔbɔ gbãtɔ bena woawɔ dɔ le aʋawo megbe.
text_en: Doctors began to be recruited by Emperor Augustus and even formed the first Roman Medical Corps for use in the aftermath of battles.

text: Amekolawo nya nu tso alɔ̃dɔtikewo abe morphine si woɖe tso poppy kuwo me kple scopolamine si woɖe tso herbane kuwo me.
text_en: Surgeons had knowledge of various sedatives including morphine from extracts of poppy seeds and scopolamine from herbane seeds.

text: Wovabi le abɔ kple ata lãla me ale be woakpe ɖe dɔnɔwo ŋu be womagalé abi vɔ̃ dɔ o; wogabi le abiblanuwo kpakple mɔ̃ si kpena ɖe woŋu be woaxe mɔ na ʋu ƒe tsatsa la wɔwɔ me.
text_en: They became proficient at amputation to save patients from gangrene as well as tourniquets and arterial clamps to stem blood flow.

text: Le ƒe alafa geɖewo me la, Roma fiaɖuƒe la na be viɖe geɖe va atikewɔwɔ me eye wòtu nu siwo míenya egbe la ɖo.
text_en: Over multiple centuries, the Roman empire led to great gains in the field of medicine and formed much of the knowledge we know today.

text: Pureland origami nye origami si ƒe see nye be ele be woaŋlɔ agbalẽa zi ɖeka ko le eŋlɔɣi, womate ŋu azã agbalẽ ŋlɔmɔnu siwo lɔ nu bubuwo ɖe eme abe agbalẽŋɔŋlɔ yi megbe o, eye akpa ɖeka dzi tẽe ko woŋloa nu sia nu le.
text_en: Pureland origami is origami with the restriction that only one fold may be done at a time, more complex folds like reverse folds are not allowed, and all folds have straightforward locations.

text: John Smith nye ame si hee doe le ƒe 1970 wo me be yeakpe ɖe ame siwo menya nu tso agbalẽ ŋɔŋlɔ ŋu o alo ame siwo ƒe aɖaŋuwo mede ŋgɔ tututu o.
text_en: It was developed by John Smith in the 1970s to help inexperienced folders or those with limited motor skills.

text: Ɖeviwo nyaa nu tso afi si wotso kple ale si amewo kpɔa afima tɔwo nenye be wole sue ko eye nukpɔkpɔ sia ƒomeviwo wɔa dɔ ɖe woƒe agbenɔnɔ dzi.
text_en: Children develop an awareness of race and racial stereotypes quite young and these racial stereotypes affect behavior.

text: Le kpɔɖeŋu me nenye be ɖeviwo tso teƒe aɖe si amewo buna be afi ma tɔwo mewɔna dɔ nyui le suku o la, ɖevi sia hã mawɔ dɔ nyui le suku nenye be ese nya sia o.
text_en: For instance, children who identify with a racial minority that is stereotyped as not doing well in school tend to not do well in school once they learn about the stereotype associated with their race.

text: MySpace lé nɔƒe etɔliã le nyatakakadzraɖoƒe siwo le United States la, eye ame miliɔn 54 yae tsɔ wo ŋutinyatakakawo da ɖe afi ma.
text_en: MySpace is the third most popular website used in the United States and has 54 million profiles currently.

text: Ame geɖewo ƒe susu vale nyatakakadzraɖoƒe siawo ŋu, vevietɔ le sukunusɔsrɔ̃ ƒe akpa dzi.
text_en: These websites have gotten a lot of attention, especially in the education setting.

text: Nyuiƒewo le nyatakakadzraɖoƒe siawo ŋu, abe ŋutete be ame naɖo eya ŋutɔ ƒe nyatakakadzraɖoƒe le internet dzi, si lɔ nuŋlɔɖiwo,videowo, nɔmetatawo kple nu bubuwo
text_en: There are positive aspects to these websites, which include, being able to easily setup a class page which can include blogs, videos, photos, and other features.

text: Woate ŋu ayi ɖe Internet-xa sia dzi to nyatakakadzraɖoƒe dzeside nana me; esia wɔnae bɔbɔe na sukuvi siwo akpe fu le kɔmpiuta kpeviwo zazã alo dzeside siawo ŋɔŋlɔ me ŋu be woaɖo ŋku edzi eye woagate ŋu aƒoe de eme bɔbɔe.
text_en: This page can easily be accessed by providing just one web address, which makes it easy to remember and easy to type in for students who may have trouble using the keyboard or with spelling.

text: Woate ŋu adzrae ɖo tɔxɛ ale be wòanɔ bɔbɔe na xexlẽ eye woagate ŋu atsɔ amadede vovovowo alo amadede sue ale si dze atsɔ aɖo atsyɔ̃e.
text_en: It can be customized to make it easy to read and also with as much or little color as desired.

text: Susu ƒe Nuŋumanɔmanɔdɔ "nye ahɔhɔ̃ me dɔléle si ƒe dzesi etɔ̃wo koŋ nye nuwɔwɔ tamemabumabutɔe, susumaɖonuŋu kpakple nuwo wɔwɔ gbodogbodoe."
text_en: Attention Deficit Disorder "is a neurological syndrome whose classic defining triad of symptoms including impulsivity, distractibility, and hyperactivity or excess energy".

text: Menye nusɔsrɔ̃ ƒe mɔxenue wònye o ke koŋ enye tɔtɔtɔ le nusɔsrɔ̃ me; ɖevi 3 va se ɖe 5 ɖe mama alafa dzi tona esia me, ɖewomahĩ Amerika viwo miliɔn 2 sɔŋ.
text_en: It is not a learning disability, it is a learning disorder; it "affects 3 to 5 percent of all children, perhaps as many as 2 million American children".

text: Esesẽ na ɖevi siwo ŋu ADD (Susu ƒe Nuŋumanɔmanɔdɔ) le la be woƒe susu nenɔ sukudɔ ŋu, ke woƒe susu ate ŋu anɔ nu siwo wɔwɔ dona dzidzɔ na wo abe fefewɔwɔ alo woƒe cartoon veviwo kpɔkpɔ alo nyagbewo ŋɔŋlɔ dzesiwo mademade wo me.
text_en: Children with ADD have a hard time focusing on things like school work, but they can concentrate on things they enjoy doing like playing games or watching their favorite cartoons or writing sentences without punctuation.

text: Ɖevi siawo hena kuxiwo vana wo ɖokuiwo dzi elabena wowɔa "nu gbodogbodo, wɔa avu hetsina tsitre ɖe nunɔlawo ŋu" ale be woƒe susu me nenyɔ, ɖe ale si womate ŋu akpɔ nyɔnyɔ le woƒe susu me abe ale si dzɔdzɔme ɖoe ene o ta.
text_en: These children tend to get into a lot of trouble, because they "engage in risky behaviors, get into fights, and challenge authority" in order to stimulate their brain, since their brain can not be stimulated by normal methods.

text: Susu ƒe Nuŋumanɔmanɔdɔ gblẽa nu le woƒe kadodo kple wo xɔlɔ̃wo ŋu elabena ɖevi bubuwo mate ŋu ase nu si ta wowɔa nu le mɔ si dzi wo wɔnɛ la dzi alo nu si ta woyɔna nyawo ƒe alfabetawo ale si woyɔnɛ alo nu si ta wowɔa nu abe ame tsitsiwo ene o.
text_en: ADD affects relationships with other peers because other children can not understand why they act the way that they do or why they spell they way they do or that their maturity level is different.

text: Abe ale si nunyanya xɔxɔ kple nusɔsrɔ̃ ƒe mɔnu trɔ le mɔ si nu míeƒo nu tsoe dzi la, ale si gbegbe amewo nya nui hã trɔ.
text_en: As the ability to obtain knowledge and to learn changed in such a way as mentioned above the base rate at which knowledge was obtained changed.

text: Mɔ si dzi wotona xɔna gbedeasi la trɔ. Dzizizi aɖeke meganɔ ame ƒe susu me dzi o, ke ame ƒe ŋutete hena ŋkuɖoɖo nuŋlɔɖi dzi vazu taɖodzinu la.
text_en: The approach to obtaining information was different. No longer did pressure reside within individual recall, but the ability to recall text became more of a focus.

text: Vevietɔe nye be, Ŋkuʋuʋuiɣeyiɣi la trɔ nusɔsrɔ̃ kple nunya mama ƒe mɔnu.
text_en: In essence, the Renaissance made a significant change in the approach to learning and the dissemination of knowledge.

text: Amegbetɔwo megale abe lã bubu siwo zãna woƒe asiwo hetsɔzɔna alo tsɔa agba alo dzona le atiwo dzi o.
text_en: Unlike other primates, hominids no longer use their hands in locomotion or bearing weight or swinging through the trees.

text: Chimpanzee ƒe asi kple afɔ sɔ le lolome kple didime si ɖe ale si wozãna asi hena nuwo tsɔtsɔ le asikɔezɔli me fia.
text_en: The chimpanzee's hand and foot are similar in size and length, reflecting the hand's use for bearing weight in knuckle walking.

text: Amegbetɔ ƒe asi le kpuie wu afɔ la tɔ, eye asibidɛ ƒuwo dzɔ wu afɔbidɛ ƒuwo tɔ.
text_en: The human hand is shorter than the foot, with straighter phalanges.

text: Ƒu xoxo aɖe si xɔ abe ƒe miliɔn eve va se ɖe ƒe miliɔn etɔ̃ ɖe ale si wotrɔ tso asi zazã hena zɔzɔ va asizazã hena nuwo wɔwɔ me fia.
text_en: Fossil hand bones two million to three million years old reveal this shift in specialization of the hand from locomotion to manipulation.

text: Amewo buna be drɔ̃e si me ame ŋutɔ nyana le be yele drɔ̃e ku le la dzɔna to xexemenuwɔwɔwo dzi, eye nenye be numetoto sia dzɔna edzi edzi la, ate ŋu ahe ɖeɖiteameŋu vɛ ŋutɔ.
text_en: Some people believe that experiencing many artificially induced lucid dreams often enough can be very exhausting.

text: Edzɔna alea nenye be drɔ̃e si me ame ŋutɔ nyana le be yele drɔ̃e ku le la gbɔ ɣeyiɣi ɖoɖo si le ɣeyiŋi si me ame ƒoa aɖaba dome.
text_en: The main reason for this phenomenon is the result of the lucid dreams expanding the length of time between REM states.

text: Nenye be ame ƒe aɖaƒoƒo le alɔ̃dɔdɔ me ɖiɖi le zã me la, alɔdɔdɔ si me wò ŋutilã kpɔa dzudzɔ le la hã zuna kuxi.
text_en: With fewer REMs per night, this state in which you experience actual sleep and your body recovers becomes infrequent enough to become a problem.

text: Esia hea ɖeɖiteameŋu vɛ abe ale si àfɔ miniti blaeve alo miniti blaetɔ̃ ɖe sia ɖe ahakpɔ TV ene.
text_en: This is just as exhausting as if you were to wake up every twenty or thirty minutes and watch TV.

text: Metsonu la ku ɖe ale si gbegbe wò susu dze agbagba be wòaku drɔ̃e si me ànya be yele drɔ̃e ku le zã sia zã la.
text_en: The effect is dependent on how often your brain attempts to lucidly dream per night.

text: Nuwo meyi edzi nyuie na Italiatɔ siwo nɔ Dzigbe Afrika tso gɔmedzedzea ke kloe o. Le abe kɔsiɖa ɖeka me, le Italy ƒe aʋahoho le Kele 10, 1940 me la, Britania tɔwo ƒe Aʋawɔla 11liawo xɔ Fort Capuzzo le Libya kple akpasesẽ.
text_en: Things did not go well for the Italians in North Africa almost from the start. Within a week of Italy's declaration of war on June 10, 1940, the British 11th Hussars had seized Fort Capuzzo in Libya.

text: Britaintɔwo lé Italytɔwo ƒe asrafowo Mɔ̃ɖaŋuŋutinyala gã Ewolia , General Lastucci, le axadeƒe si le Bardia ƒe ɣedzeƒe la.
text_en: In an ambush east of Bardia, the British captured the Italian Tenth Army's Engineer-in-Chief, General Lastucci.

text: Le Masa 28 me la, xɔlɔ̃ tukpe si woda Marshal Italo Balbo, Libya tɔwo ƒe Dukplɔla Gã kple Mussolini ƒe domenyila, le esime eƒe yameʋu nɔ dzedzem le Tobruk la wui.
text_en: On June 28, Marshal Italo Balbo, the Governor-General of Libya and apparent heir to Mussolini, was killed by friendly fire while landing in Tobruk.

text: Đoƒe geɖewoe wowͻa egbe lãmesefefewo si nye yinuve dada le, tso sukuvi siwo le nu srͻm le sukukͻkͻ me va se ɖe duta hoטiטliwo me.
text_en: The modern sport of fencing is played at many levels, from students learning at a university to professional and Olympic competition.

text: oƒe geɖewoe wowͻa egbe lãmesefefewo le, tso sukuvi siwo le nu srͻm le sukukͻkͻ me va se ɖe duta hoטiטliwo me.
text_en: The sport is primarily played in a duel format, one fencer dueling another.

text: Golf nye fefe si aboƒolawo zãna ati legbewo tsͻ zinɛ de doawo me.
text_en: Golf is a game in which players use clubs to hit balls into holes.

text: Dada wuiͻenyie yia dzi le fefea me. Ame si dze dada gbãtͻ gͻme tso do gbãtͻ dzi la wua nu ɖe do wui enyilia dzi.
text_en: Eighteen holes are played during a regular round, with players usually starting on the first hole on the course and finishing on the eighteenth.

text: Ame si tsoa ati ƒe agbͻsͻsͻ si le sͻe tsͻ wu dadawo katã nu la zua dziɖula.
text_en: The player who takes the fewest strokes, or swings of the club, to complete the course wins.

text: Hoטiטli sia yina edzi le sͻ gbe dzi, eye woŋlͻa sͻgbe siwo ƒ xlã do si me fefe la yina edzi wozua kpuie.
text_en: The game is played on grass, and the grass around the hole is mown shorter and called the green.

text: Mͻzͻz va nye modzakaɖenu bͻbͻ kekeake: Asitͻtrͻ le modzakatsaɖiƒewo ŋu.
text_en: Perhaps the most common type of tourism is what most people associate with traveling: Recreation tourism.

text: Esiae nye ne amewo yi teƒe swoi to vovo na teƒe siwo wonͻna gbawo tsyo gbe be yewoado dzidzͻ ɖe yewo ɖokui ŋu.
text_en: This is when people go to a place that is very different from their regular day-to-day life to relax and have fun.

text: ƒutawo, gbadza dzi siwo wͻna tͻxɛwo yia edzi le lae modzakatsaɖilawo te ŋu va na.
text_en: Beaches, theme parks and camp grounds are often the most common places frequented by recreational tourists.

text: Ne ame aɖe ƒe taɖodzie nye be yeanya nu tso tsãnudzͻdzͻ siwo ku ɖe teƒe si yeɖi tsa va ŋu la, ke modzakatsaɖiɖi sia nye dekͻnu mͻzͻzͻ.
text_en: If the objective of one’s visit to a particular place is to get to know its history and culture then this type of tourism is known as cultural tourism.

text: Modzakatsaɖilawo ate ŋu aɖi tsa ade dukͻ ƒe akpa geɖe alo woate ŋu ato mo ɖe teƒe ɖeka ko ŋu.
text_en: Tourists may visit different landmarks of a particular country or they may simply opt to focus on just one area.

text: Ne dukͻdziɖulawo kpͻ wͻna siawo la, wodea woƒoa abͻta na wo.
text_en: The Colonists, seeing this activity, had also called for reinforcements.

text: Ameha siwo nͻ ŋgͻgbe na ɖoɖo siawo dometͻ aɖewoe nye ame 200 le Hampshire ƒe dziɖuɖu 1tͻ kple 3liawo le John Stark kple James Reed ƒe dziɖuɖu te.
text_en: Troops reinforcing the forward positions included the 1st and 3rd New Hampshire regiments of 200 men, under Colonels John Stark and James Reed (both later became generals).

text: Stark ƒe amewo xͻ ɖoƒe le dukͻdziɖulawo ƒe dziɖuɖu nuwuwu le ɣedzeƒe.
text_en: Stark's men took positions along the fence on the north end of the Colonist's position.

text: Ne amu ƒe agbodzedze he טu le tͻsisiwo ŋu ɣedzeƒe le, wokeke kpͻtͻtͻwo ƒo xlã ekpekui gliwo kͻ yi ɣedzeƒe si le tͻ nu la.
text_en: When low tide opened a gap along the Mystic River along the northeast of the peninsula, they quickly extended the fence with a short stone wall to the north ending at the water's edge on a small beach.

text: Gridley alo Stark de ati abe afͻ 100 (30m) ƒe didime ene le kpͻtͻtͻ la ƒe ŋgͻ gbe eye woɖe gbe be ame aɖeke megagble edome o.
text_en: Gridley or Stark placed a stake about 100 feet (30 m) in front of the fence and ordered that no one fire until the regulars passed it.

text: Amerikatͻwo ɖo dzi ɖe ɖoɖowͻwͻ be yewoaho aטa tso mͻ vovovo etͻ dzi.
text_en: The American plan relied on launching coordinated attacks from three different directions.

text: John Cadwalder aho aטa si ade mama British yevuawo dome le Borden du me kple susu be yeaɖo asi abͻtaƒoƒo ɖe sia ɖe dzi.
text_en: General John Cadwalder would launch a diversionary attack against the British garrison at Bordentown, in order to block off any reinforcements.

text: James Ewing aho aטa kple gbadagba 700 sͻ ɖe Trenton tͻ to, axe mͻ le Assunpink Creek ahaxe mͻ na futͻwo be womagasi o.
text_en: General James Ewing would take 700 militia across the river at Trenton Ferry, seize the bridge over the Assunpink Creek and prevent any enemy troops from escaping.

text: Hunyahunyawͻla 2,400 ya atso tͻ la ava do ɖe Trenton ɣetoɖoƒe eye woama ɖe hatsotso eve me, akpa ɖeka nanͻ Greene eye akpa evelia nanͻ Sullivan, kple susu be woaho aטa do ŋgͻe.
text_en: The main assault force of 2,400 men would cross the river nine miles north of Trenton, and then split into two groups, one under Greene and one under Sullivan, in order to launch a pre-dawn attack.

text: Esime wonye nuwo le tͻtrͻm ta la, dzitsitsi meganye nu si le vevie o, ke ameɖokuidziɖuɖu kple kutrikukue le vevie.
text_en: With the change from the quarter to the half mile run, speed becomes of much less importance and endurance becomes an absolute necessity.

text: Nyateƒee wonye be duƒula si ate ŋu aƒu du le aɖabaƒoƒo eve me la, hiã na wͻwͻ ɖe game dzi ƒe gbͻgbͻ ma, gake ameɖokuidziɖuɖu hiã le gowo katã me.
text_en: Of course a first-class half-miler, a man who can beat two minutes, must be possessed of a fair amount of speed, but endurance must be cultivated at all hazards.

text: Dulegbeƒuƒule tle tsidzaŋͻli hekpe ɖe lãmesĕdͻwͻwͻ ɖe amegbetͻ ƒe dziƒo gbͻ lae nye dzadzraɖo adodoea le duƒuɣi.
text_en: Some cross country running during the winter, combined with gymnasium work for the upper part of the body, is the best preparation for the running season.

text: Nuɖuɖu nyuiwo ɖuɖu ɖeɖe dzaa mate ŋu awͻe be woakpͻ dzidzedze o, gake akpe ɖe duƒula sueawo ŋu le woƒe lãmesenyawo me.
text_en: Proper nutritional practices alone cannot generate elite performances, but they can significantly affect young athletes' overall wellness.

text: Belele na ame ƒe lãmese, tsinono ãe game dzi kple dedienͻnͻnyawo gͻmesese ate ŋu akpe.
text_en: Maintaining a healthy energy balance, practicing effective hydration habits, and understanding the various aspects of supplementation practices can help athletes improve their performance and increase their enjoyment of the sport.

text: Du kpui ƒuƒu mexͻ asi o, ke nyamaɖinya aɖewo li ku ɖe dͻwͻnu siwo hiã be woazã hena gomekpͻkpͻ le me.
text_en: Middle distance running is a relatively inexpensive sport; however, there are many misconceptions regarding the few pieces of equipment required to participate.

text: Woate ŋu akpͻ nuawo aƒle gake geɖe mahe tͻtrͻ aɖeke vɛ o.
text_en: Products can be purchased as needed, but most will have little or no real impact on performance.

text: Hɛllawo axͻe se be yewolͻa nane ne viɖɛ aɖeke mado go tso eme hã o.
text_en: Athletes may feel that they prefer a product even when it provides no real benefits.

text: Wode dzesi atͻmuwo abe nu siwo wͻ nu sia nu la ƒe gͻmeɖokpewo ɖeka ene.
text_en: The atom can be considered to be one of the fundamental building blocks of all matter.

text: Enye nu kplͻhͻ aɖe si le Borh ƒe susuɖaŋu nu la, eƒe amikɛ alo dzi [nucleus] nye nu si amikɛviwo [electrons] le xlã ƒomee abe ale si anygbahawo alo planɛtiwo nͻ xlã ƒom ɣee ene. kpͻ Tata 1.1.
text_en: Its a very complex entity which consists, according to a simplified Bohr model, of a central nucleus orbited by electrons, somewhat similar to planets orbiting the sun - see Figure 1.1.

text: Nu kui eve ƒo ƒu wͻ nuwo ƒe amikɛ alo dzi siwo nye ŋusĕmanͻsitͻwo alo nitrͻniwo kple ŋusĕɖealͻtͻwo alo protͻniwo.
text_en: The nucleus consists of two particles - neutrons and protons.

text: Protͻniwo la, ŋusĕɖealͻ le wo me ke nitrͻniwo la, ŋusĕ aɖeke mele wo me o. Nu kui etͻli si nye eletrͻni la, ŋusĕmaɖealͻe le eme.
text_en: Protons have a positive electric charge while neutrons have no charge. The electrons have a negative electric charge.

text: Hafi nakpͻ ame si dzi nua dzͻ ɖo la, ele be nale ŋku ɖe teƒea hena wo dedienͻnͻ.
text_en: To Check the victim, you must first survey the scene to ensure your safety.

text: Ele be nade dzesi ame si dzi nua dz ɖo ƒe nͻnͻme le esime nele tetem ɖe eŋu.
text_en: You need to notice the victim's position as you approach him or her and any automatic red flags.

text: Ne ekpͻ afͻku le esime nele agbagba dzem be yeakpe ɖe ame aɖe ŋu la, ɖe ko nagadzi fu ɖe edzi.
text_en: If you get hurt trying to help, you may only serve to make matters worse.

text: Nusͻsrͻ nugͻmekuku ɖee fia be tamebubudͻlele kple vͻvͻ ɖe kadodo si le vevesese kple nuwͻmee dome le vevesese si le alime gbͻ le ame ƒe dzimegbe.
text_en: The study found that depression, fear and catastrophising mediated the relationship between pain and disability in lower back pain sufferers.

text: Susumadzeanyi ƒe nugbleƒe ko, menye tamebubu kple vͻvͻe nye esiwo ɖea fu ɣe sia ɣi o.
text_en: Only the effects of catastrophizing, not depression and fear was conditional of regular weekly structured PA sessions.

text: Ame siwo ƒoa wo ɖokuiwo ɖe gbe sia gbe dͻwͻnawo me la hiãna kpekpeɖeŋu ku ɖe susu baɖa siwo vana woƒe susu me ɖe ale si womete ŋu dea vovototo dͻlele vͻɖiɖwo kple dzimaɖeɖi siwo wodoa goe le teƒe si medze dzi na wo me o.
text_en: Those participating in regular activity required more support in terms of negative perception of pain distinguishing the differences of chronic pain and discomfort feel from normal physical movement.

text: Nukpͻkpͻ tsoa miaƒe nukpͻkpͻkpɛxͻnuwo alo ŋkuwo gbͻ.
text_en: Vision, or the ability to see depends on visual system sensory organs or eyes.

text: Nͻnͻme vovovowoe le ŋku si eye etso sesĕtͻ dzi va yi gblͻetͻ dzi eye eku ɖe nugbagbe si ƒe lãme wole.
text_en: There are many different constructions of eyes, ranging in complexity depending on the requirements of the organism.

text: Nͻnͻme ɖe sia ɖe kple eƒe ŋutetee, wohiã na wozazã le mͻnu vovovowo dzi kple susu be taɖodzinu si dim wole la nawͻ dͻ.
text_en: The different constructions have different capabilities, are sensitive to different wave-lengths and have differing degrees of acuity, also they require different processing to make sense of the input and different numbers to work optimally.

text: Hatsotso nye nu gbagbe siwo le ha ɖeka me le teƒe aɖe.
text_en: A population is the collection of organisms of a particular species within a given geographic area.

text: Ne nu siwo le hatsotso ɖeka me la nye nu ɖekawo alo ɖi wo nͻewo la, le ƒomedodzesi ɖeka aɖe ƒe dzidzeti nu la, wonye dzͻdzͻmeɖeka nuwo.
text_en: When all individuals in a population are identical with regard to a particular phenotypic trait they are known as monomorphic.

text: Ne nu siwo le hatsotso ɖeka me la meɖi wo nͻewo le ƒomedodzesi ɖeka aɖe ƒe dzidzeti nu o la, wonye dzͻdzͻmevovo nuwo.
text_en: When the individuals show several variants of a particular trait they are polymorphic.

text: Agbasrɛwo ɖea abͻ eye wowͻa atͻ le nͻnͻme vovovowo me.
text_en: Army ant colonies march and nest in different phases as well.

text: L woƒe tsatsa me la, agbasrɛwo zͻna le zã me eye wotͻna ɖoa xͻ le ŋkeke me.
text_en: In the nomadic phase, army ants march at night and stop to camp during the day.

text: Wodzena tsatsa gͻme nenye be nuɖuɖu si lee la sͻ agbͻ, wowͻna atͻ aɖe si woɖͻli na gbe sia gbe.
text_en: The colony begins a nomadic phase when available food has decreased. During this phase, the colony makes temporary nests that are changed everyday.

text: Tsaɖiɖi siawo wua nu abe le ŋkeke 17 me ene.
text_en: Each of these nomadic rampages or marches lasts for approximately 17 days.

text: Nu kae nye lãmetuɖoka (cell)? Nya cell do go tso Latin nya cella me, si gͻmee nye xͻ sue, amesiwo kpͻna nu suetͻ kekeakewo woe de dzesie gbã.
text_en: What is a cell? The word cell comes from the Latin word "cella", meaning "small room", and it was first coined by a microscopist observing the structure of cork.

text: Lãmetuɖoka nye nugbagbe ɖe sia ɖe ƒe agbe ƒe gͻmeɖɛkpe, eye ɖeka alo wu la nͻa nu gbagbe ɖe sia ɖe me.
text_en: The cell is the basic unit of all living things, and all organisms are composed of one or more cells.

text: Lãmetuɖokawo nye nu vevi aɖe si ŋu wolea ŋku ɖo le nusͻsrͻ tso agbe ŋu me ale gbegbe be woyͻna wo be agbetutu ƒe kpe.
text_en: Cells are so basic and critical to the study of life, in fact, that they are often referred to as "the building blocks of life".

text: Miaƒe lameטuka siwo nana be miewͻna nu sia nu la kpena ɖe mia ŋu be טu nate ŋu aɖe zͻ le miaƒe lãme ade teƒe siwo katã wohiã be טu nade.
text_en: The Nervous System maintains homeostasis by sending nerve impulses through out the body to keep the flow of blood going as well as undisturbed.

text: טuka siawo ate ŋu akaka ɖe miaƒe lãme katã si kpena ɖe mia ŋu be mienͻa lãmese me eye wogaxea mͻ na nu manyomanyowo siwo ava do mo ɖa hã.
text_en: These nerve impulses can be sent so quickly throughout the body which helps keep the body safe from any potential threat.

text: Le ahomu yawo katã dome la, Tomadoes nye esi gblea nu le teƒe sue aɖe ko, gake egblea nu sia nu si le eƒe mͻ me la.
text_en: Tornadoes strike a small area compared to other violent storms, but they can destroy everything in their path.

text: Ahomuya Tomadoes hoa atiwo, xͻwo eye wokoa טuwo sia yia yame.Tomadoes mama ɖe alafa dzi teƒe eve yia dzi wu gaƒoƒo etͻ.
text_en: Tornadoes uproot trees, rip boards from buildings, and fling cars up into the sky. The most violent two percent of tornadoes last more than three hours.

text: Ahomu vͻɖi siawo 480 km/h (133 m/s; 300 mph).
text_en: These monster storms have winds up to 480 km/h (133 m/s; 300 mph).

text: Amegbetͻ nͻa nukpͻgaŋkui zãm le nu geɖe wͻwͻ me abe ƒe akpe akpewo ene.
text_en: Humans have been making and using lenses for magnification for thousands and thousands of years.

text: Ke wowͻ adzͻgenukpͻmͻ gbãtͻ le Europa dukͻ me le ƒe akpe ɖeka alafa wuiade 16 mawo ƒe nuwuwu me.
text_en: However, the first true telescopes were made in Europe in the late 16th century.

text: Adzͻgenukpͻmͻ sia zã nukpͻgaŋkui eve tsͻ wͻa nu siwo le adzͻge טii la wotena ɖe ame ŋu helolo na.
text_en: These telescopes used a combination of two lenses to make distant objects appear both nearer and larger.

text: ŋubia kple ame ɖokuit didi ɖe woko anyi nͻ ge kplee mi ɖaa eye dzͻdzͻme ƒe see wonye be ne ame akpa gãtͻ kpͻ viɖɛ la, ɖokuitͻdidi ana be woakpͻe le agbͻsͻsͻ me le ɣeyiɣi kpui aɖe me.
text_en: Greed and selfishness will always be with us and it is the nature of cooperation that when the majority benefit there will always be more to gain in the short term by acting selfishly

text: Egbͻna amewo ŋu dze ge gbe ɖeka be, tiatia nyuitͻe nye be tewoawͻ dͻ kple ame bubuwo.
text_en: Hopefully, most people will realise that their long term best option is to work together with others.

text: Ame aɖewo kua drͻe ku ɖe gbe si gbe amegbetͻ nazͻ mͻ ayi ɖe teƒei bubuwo ahaɖi tsa le xexea ƒe akpa sia akpa, ame aɖewo mesea nu si tututue le teƒe mawo o, ame aɖew bui be agbenͻnͻ bubuwo anͻ xexea ƒe teƒe bubu .
text_en: Many people dream of the day when humans can travel to another star and explore other worlds, some people wonder what's out there some belive that aliens or other life may live on another plant.

text: Gake ne esia ava dzͻ hã, manͻ anyi didi o. ɣletiviwo kakana ɖe teƒe ɖe sia ɖe.
text_en: But, if this ever does happen probably won't happen for a very long time. The stars are so spread out that there are trillions of miles between stars that are "neighbors".

text: Đe wo ma hi, wo dzidzimeviwo anͻ atsitre ɖe teƒe aɖe abe amedzro ene anͻ tame bum tso wo tͻgbeawo ŋu gbe ɖeka.
text_en: Maybe one day, your great grandchildren will be standing atop an alien world wondering about their ancient ancestors?

text: Lãmetuɖoka geɖewoe le lãwo me. Woɖua nu eye wodzea anyi ɖe lãme na wo. Lã geɖewo ate ŋu azͻ.
text_en: Animals are made of many cells. They eat things and digest them inside. Most animals can move.

text: Lãwo si ko susu le (togbͻ be menye lãwo katãe; le kpͻɖeŋu me, susu mele tͻmelã si woyͻna be dzidzi si o.
text_en: Only animals have brains (though not even all animals do; jellyfish, for example, do not have brains).

text: Lãwo le anyigbadzi godoo. Woɖea טe ɖe anyigba me, ƒua tsi le tͻ gãwo me, eye wodzona le yame.
text_en: Animals are found all over the earth. They dig in the ground, swim in the oceans, and fly in the sky.

text: Lãmetuɖoka nye nu suetͻ kekeake si wͻa dͻ le nugbagbewo me.
text_en: A cell is the smallest structural and functional unit of a living (things) organism.

text: Lãmetuɖoka (cell) do tso Latin gbe cella me si gͻmee nye xͻ sue.
text_en: Cell comes from the Latin word cella which means small room.

text: Ne ekpͻ nugbagbe kple adzͻgenukpͻmͻ la, akpͻe be wole sue abe bͻlͻviwo ene.
text_en: If you look at living things under a microscope, you will see that they are made of small squares or balls.

text: Robert Hooke, nugbagbeŋutinunyala si tso England dukͻ me kpͻ xͻvi suesuewo le kͻŋki me kple adzͻgenukpͻmͻ.
text_en: Robert Hooke, a biologist from England, saw small squares in cork with a microscope.

text: Wodze abe xͻe ene. Eyae nye ame gbãtͻ si le ŋku ɖe lãmetuɖoka kukuwo.
text_en: They looked like rooms. He was the first person to observe dead cells

text: Nu siawo ɖea zͻ tso ɖeka dzi va yia evelia dzi eye wometrͻna nͻnͻme o.
text_en: Elements and compounds can move from one state to another and not change.

text: Ya si si טeטe kple dzedzeme aɖeke mele o la ɖe ko wosͻ kple tsitͻ hã.Kpekpe nͻa tsi ƒe nͻnͻmetͻ ŋu wu gake nu siwo e wo me sͻ.
text_en: Nitrogen as a gas still has the same properties as liquid nitrogen. The liquid state is denser but the molecules are still the same.

text: Tsie nye kpͻɖeŋu bubu. Ya si doa go tso amegbetͻ me si atͻm ewe wͻ kple ya si amegbetͻ gbͻna si atͻm ɖeka koe wͻe.
text_en: Water is another example. The compound water is made up of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

text: Nͻnͻme ɖeka koe le esi, eɖanye tsi, ya alo kpetͻ.
text_en: It has the same molecular structure whether it is a gas, liquid, or solid.

text: Togbͻ be eƒe dzedzeme atrͻ hã, nu siwo le eme la anͻ neema ko.
text_en: Although its physical state may change, its chemical state remains the same.

text: ɣeyiɣi nye nane si le mía gbͻ, eye wowͻa dͻ ɖe nu sia nu si míewͻna dzi, gake egͻme menyase na o.
text_en: Time is something that is all around us, and affects everything we do, yet is difficult to understand.

text: Nunyalagãwo, subͻsubͻwo kple dzͻdzͻmeŋutinunyalawo srͻ nu tso ɣeyiɣi ŋu ƒe akpewo
text_en: Time has been studied by religious, philosophical, and scientific scholars for thousands of years.

text: Míekpͻa ɣeyiɣi abe ale si nudzͻdzͻ vovovova yina tso tsã va yi fifi me.
text_en: We experience time as a series of events passing from the future through the present to the past.

text: ɣeyiɣi kee ganye ale si miebua nudzͻdzͻ ƒe didimee.
text_en: Time is also how we compare the duration (length) of events.

text: Wo ŋutͻ ate ŋu ade dzesi ɣeyiɣi ɖokuiwo si to ŋkulele ɖe nudzͻdzͻ siwo yia edzi enuenu ŋu. Nudzͻdzͻ siawo nye nu siwo dzͻna gadzͻna ake atraɖie.
text_en: You can mark the passing of time yourself by observing the repetition of a cyclical event. A cyclical event is something that happens again and again regularly.

text: Egbe ŋkuטuטui mͻɖaŋuwo trͻna asi le nͻnͻmetatawo ŋu.
text_en: Computers today are used to manipulate pictures and videos.

text: Nͻnͻmetata dzeatsyͻ siwo wowͻna to aɖaŋu blibo me le mͻɖaŋuwozazã me la le agbͻ sͻm le tiviwo dzi .
text_en: Sophisticated animations can be constructed on computers, and this kind of animation is increasingly being used in television and films.

text: Wowͻna hagbewo hele nɛdana ɖi to ŋkuטuטui mͻɖaŋuwo zazã me.
text_en: Music is often recorded using sophisticated computers to process and mix sounds together.

text: Tso gbe aɖe gbe ke la, amegbatͻ siwo nͻ Zealand la nye Maoritͻ siwo dea adegbe na xevi gãwo wuwu.
text_en: For a long time during the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, it was believed the first inhabitants of New Zealand were the Maori people, who hunted giant birds called moas.

text: Nugͻmekuku ɖee fia be susu ma be Maoritͻwo טu tso Polynesia le agbͻsͻsͻ me eye wova xͻ Zealand dukͻa le Morioritͻwo si hetse wͻ agbledede kple lãnyiƒee.
text_en: The theory then established the idea that the Maori people migrated from Polynesia in a Great Fleet and took New Zealand from the Moriori, establishing an agricultural society.

text: Ke nyateƒe ɖee fia beMorioritͻwo nye Maoritͻwo ƒe hatsotso si טu tso Zealand duyeye vaɖo Chatham Tͻdomenyigba dzi eye wowͻ wo ŋutͻ wo ɖokuiwo ƒe ŋutifafa nuɖoanyiwo.
text_en: However, new evidence suggests that the Moriori were a group of mainland Maori who migrated from New Zealand to the Chatham Islands, developing their own distinctive, peaceful culture.

text: Gbegbͻgbkͻ bubu gblͻla aɖewo le Catham nyigba nyi woe nye Maoriͻ siwo טu tso Zealand dukͻ me.
text_en: There was also another tribe on the Chatham islands these were Maori who migrated away from New Zealand.

text: Woyͻ wo ɖokuiwo be Morioritͻwo, masͻmasͻ vi aɖewo geɖe wo dome, eye le nuwuwua, woɖe Morioritͻwo ɖa.
text_en: They called themselves the Moriori there were a few skirmishes and in the end, the Moriori were wiped out

text: Ame ɖekaɖeka siwo kpͻ wo ɖokuiwo le nudzͻdzͻ vovovowo me la kpena ɖe mía ŋu be míedea dzesi nu siwo míewͻna nyuie kple nu siwo le mía me ne míele ŋku lem ɖe nukpekeamewo kple numadzedziwoŋu gͻ hã.
text_en: Individuals who had been involved for several decades helped us appreciate our strengths and passions while candidly assessing difficulties and even failures.

text: Ne míele to ɖom amewo wole nu ƒom tso woƒe numetotowo tso woƒe ƒome kple woƒe dͻwͻƒewo ŋu la, eטua míaƒe ŋkuwo ɖe nu siwo dzͻ va yi kple ame ave siwo wͻ dͻ ve míadzi le nyui kple gbegblewo sia me.
text_en: While listening to individuals share their individual, family, and organizational stories, we gained valuable insight into the past and some of the personalities who influenced for good or ill the culture of the organization.

text: Ame ave ƒe dzͻtsoƒe gͻmesese mefia be amea nya nu tso eƒe dekͻnu ŋu o ke ekpena ɖe wo ŋu be woanya nu tso afi si woƒe wͻƒe le dͻwͻƒe alo habͻbͻa me.
text_en: While understanding one’s history does not assume understanding of culture, it does at least help people gain a sense of where they fall within the history of the organization.

text: Ne wo ŋku lem ɖe dzidzedzekpͻkpͻwo hele ŋku טum ɖe nukpekeamewo ŋu la, ame ɖekɛ ɖekɛwo kple ame siwo katã le ɖe tsͻm le dͻwͻƒea me la ƒe ŋku טuna ɖe dͻwͻƒea ƒe kpekpeme, tsͻmekpͻŋku kple nu siwo adoe ɖe ŋgͻ ŋuti.
text_en: While assessing the successes and becoming aware of failures, individuals and the whole of the participating persons discover more deeply the values, mission, and driving forces of the organization.

text: Le kpͻɖeŋu sia me la, ŋkuɖoɖo nu siwo dzͻ va vi dzi le agbenͻnͻ siwo yi dzi le dͻwͻna me si na dzidzedzekpͻkpͻ la kpena ɖe sͻlemea ŋu be tͻtrͻ yeyewo va na hena wo dada ɖe mͻ dzi.
text_en: In this instance, recalling previous instances of entrepreneurial behavior and resulting successes helped people to be open to new changes and new direction for the local church.

text: ŋutinya mawo ɖea vͻvͻ dzi kpͻtͻ na, ne ɖoɖo nyuiwo le edzi yim hena tͻtrͻ le etsͻme.
text_en: Such success stories lessened the fears of change, while creating positive inclinations toward change in the future.

text: Tamebubu le mɔ vovovowo nu nye aɖaŋumɔ si dzi wotona hea ŋuɖoɖowo vae na kuxiwo eye to edzi la, woƒoa tamesusu vovovowo nu ƒu ale be woakpɔ ŋuɖoɖo.
text_en: Convergent thinking patterns are problem solving techniques that unite different ideas or fields to find a solution.

text: Tamesusu sia ƒe taɖodzinue nye ablaɖeɖe, nuwo ŋu bubu nyuie kple nuwo ƒe blibodede. Ke hã dzesidede nu siwo li, aɖaŋu siwo li la ŋu dɔ wɔwɔ ake kple nyadzɔdzɔwo ƒoƒoƒu.
text_en: The focus of this mindset is speed, logic and accuracy, also identification of facts, reapplying existing techniques, gathering information.

text: Nu si bɔ le tamesusu sia ŋue nye be: ŋuɖoɖo nyui ɖeka koe li. Ɖeko àte ŋu àbu ŋuɖoɖo eve, si nye nu nyui alo nu gbegblẽ ŋu.
text_en: The most important factor of this mindset is: there is only one correct answer. You only think of two answers, namely right or wrong.

text: Tamebubu sia ƒomevi kuɖe dzɔdzɔmenuŋutinunya alo seɖoanyi aɖewo ŋu.
text_en: This type of thinking is associated with certain science or standard procedures.

text: Ame siwo si tamesusu sia tɔgbui le la bua susu eme kɔna nyuie. Ŋutete le wosi be woalé ɖoɖo siwo nu nuwo dzɔ le la ɖe tame, wote ŋu hea ŋuɖoɖowo vae na kuxiwo hegawɔa dzɔdzɔmenuŋutinunya dodokpɔwo.
text_en: People with this type of thinking have logical thinking, are able to memorize patterns, solve problems and work on scientific tests.

text: Amegbetͻwoe nye nugbagbe siwo si nunya le be woate ŋu ade dzesi nu bubuwo ƒe susu.
text_en: Humans are by far the most talented species in reading the minds of others.

text: Ema fia be míete ŋu kpͻ nu siwo ame bubuwo bu, ɖo be yewoawͻ, nya alo di la.
text_en: That means we are able to successfully predict what other humans perceive, intend, believe, know or desire.

text: Le nutete siawo dome la, ame nͻewo gͻmesese hiã vevie. Enana be míeɖͻa tukaɖa siwo ava dzͻ ɖo.
text_en: Among these abilities, understanding the intention of others is crucial. It allows us to resolve possible ambiguities of physical actions.

text: Le kpͻɖeŋu me, ne ekpͻ ame aɖe wole טu ƒe fesrɛ gbam la, atsͻe be ɖe wole agbagba dzem be yeafi amedzro aɖe ƒe טu.
text_en: For example, if you were to see someone breaking a car window, you would probably assume he was trying to steal a stranger’s car.

text: Woabu susu bubu ɖe eŋu ne ɖe wobu ye ŋutͻ ƒe טusafui eye eya ŋutͻ ƒe טu gbam wole be yeage ɖe eme.
text_en: He would need to be judged differently if he had lost his car keys and it was his own car that he was trying to break into.

text: MRI nye ŋnudzͻdzͻ aɖe si le mía dome si woyͻna be nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), si Felix Bloch (nͻ dͻ wͻm le Standard University) kple Edward Purcell (tso Harvard University) de dzesie le ƒe 1930 me.
text_en: MRI is based on a physics phenomenon called nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), which was discovered in the 1930s by Felix Bloch (working at Stanford University) and Edward Purcell (from Harvard University).

text: Le zinyenye sia mea, eletriki nulenu kple wͻlesi kawo nana be wͻlesi ƒe dzi ɖea asi le radio ƒe dzesi aɖewo ŋu.
text_en: In this resonance, magnetic field and radio waves cause atoms to give off tiny radio signals.

text: Le ƒe 1970 mea, Raymod Damadian, dͻyͻla kple dzͻdzͻmeŋutinunyala aɖe, dedzesii be nulemͻ ƒe zinyenye ƒe woanye nane si woatsͻ do dͻnͻwo kpͻe.
text_en: In the year 1970, Raymond Damadian, a medical doctor and research scientist, discovered the basis for using magnetic resonance imaging as a tool for medical diagnosis.

text: Le ƒe ene megbe la, woxͻ mͻɖeɖe, si nye mͻɖeɖe gãtͻ le xexea me le MRI ŋudͻwͻwͻ me.
text_en: Four years later a patent was granted, which was the world's first patent issued in the field of MRI.

text: Le ƒe 1977 me, Dr. Damadian wu MRI amedzidzimͻ si wogblͻ be naneke mate ŋu akpe dzi o.
text_en: In 1977, Dr. Damadian completed the construction of the first “whole-body” MRI scanner, which he called the ”Indomitable”.

text: Nuƒoƒo to yaטalazazã me nana ɣeyiɣi be ame na bu ta me hafi aɖo nya ŋu na amewo.
text_en: Asynchronous communication encourages time for reflection and reaction to others.

text: Enana sukuviwo nutete be woawͻ dͻdeaiwo le wo ɖokui si.
text_en: It allows students the ability to work at their own pace and control the pace of instructional information.

text: Gakpe ɖe eŋua, wonana ɣeyiɣi dea ame dzi be woagbͻ dzi ɖi le gaƒoƒo siwo wozãna le dͻwͻna me. (Bremer, 1998)
text_en: In addition, there are fewer time restrictions with the possibility of flexible working hours. (Bremer, 1998)

text: Mͻɖaŋu ŋutinunya zazã wͻe be nusrͻlawo kpͻa gome hexͻa nutsotso ɣeawo katã ɣi.
text_en: The use of the Internet and the World Wide Web allows learners to have access to information at all times.

text: Sukuviwo hã ate ŋu aɖo woƒe biabiawo ɖe nufialawo le ɣeyiɣi ɖe sia ɖe le vkekea me ahanͻ mͻ kpͻm na ŋuɖoɖoawo kaba tsͻ wu be woatͻ ava de asi na esime wodo go ŋkume kple ŋkume.
text_en: Students can also submit questions to instructors at any time of day and expect reasonably quick responses, rather than waiting until the next face-to-face meeting.

text: Nusͻsrͻ tso nusiwo dzͻ va yi si sͻ kple esiwo le dzͻdzͻm le fifia me nana mi ablͻɖe geɖe.
text_en: The postmodern approach to learning offers the freedom from absolutes. There is no one good way to learn.

text: Le nyateƒe mea, menye nu nyui ɖeka koe le nu sͻsrͻ me o. Nusͻsrͻ yia edzi le nuteƒekpͻkpͻ si le nusrͻla kple sidzedze si woda ɖi dome.
text_en: In fact, there is not one good thing to learn.Learning takes place in the experience between the learner and the knowledge presented.

text: Dͻwͻwͻ kple nutsotso nana le ame ɖokui si si teƒe kpͻm míele le egbea mea, nukpͻmͻwo alo tiviwo ɖea akpa sia fiana mi.
text_en: Our current experience with all the do-it-yourself and information presenting, learning-based television shows illustrates this point.

text: Mía ame geɖewo míekpͻa mía ɖokui le tivi kpͻkpͻ me siɖea nanewo kple nuteɖekpͻkpͻ aɖe siwo míele zazã ge o.
text_en: So many of us find ourselves watching a television show that informs us of a process or experience in which we will never participate or apply that knowledge.

text: Miele טu wͻ ge gbeɖe o, atu miaƒe tsidzͻƒe ɖe míaƒe kpͻ te, azͻ mͻ yi Peru aɖale ŋku ɖe nu siwo dzͻ le tsã me va yi alo atrͻ asi le m]aƒe aƒelikawo ƒe aƒe ŋu o.
text_en: We will never overhaul a car, build a fountain in our backyard, travel to Peru to examine ancient ruins, or remodel our neighbour's house.

text: Akpe na tͻgͻme eletrikika si va to Uropa dukͻme kple yaטala si wowͻ to anyigba me, Greenlight dukͻa mama ɖe alafa dzi 93 ƒe agbͻ sͻsͻ le yaטala zãm.
text_en: Thanks to undersea fiber optic cable links to Europe and broadband satellite, Greenland is well connected with 93% of the population having internet access.

text: Wo nu siwo nazã anͻ yaטala dzi la anͻ amedzrodzeƒe si nadze.
text_en: Your hotel or hosts (if staying in a guesthouse or private home) will likely have wifi or an internet connected PC, and all settlements have an internet cafe or some location with public wifi.

text: Abe ale si wogblɔe va yi ene la, togbɔ be United States xɔ ɖe nya “Eskimo” zazã dzi hã la, ame geɖe siwo menye U.S. Arctiktɔwo o, vevietɔ le Canada la, bui abe gbɔɖiamenya ene.
text_en: As mentioned above, though the word "Eskimo" remains acceptable in the United States, it is considered pejorative by many non-U.S. Arctic peoples, especially in Canada.

text: Ke esime nase nya sia zazã le Greenlandic tɔwo nu la, ele be amedzrowo naƒo asa na ezazã.
text_en: While you may hear the word used by Greenlandic Natives, its use should be avoided by foreigners.

text: Greenland dumeviwo yɔa woɖokuiwo le Canada kple Kalaalleq (ne wosɔ gbɔ la enye Kalaallit) be Inuit, Greenland tɔ aɖe, le Greenland.
text_en: The native inhabitants of Greenland call themselves Inuit in Canada and Kalaalleq (plural Kalaallit), a Greenlander, in Greenland.

text: Nu vlo wɔwɔ kple tamesesẽ ɖe amedzrowo ŋu nye nu gbadza si li, ke esesẽ alegbegbe be woakpɔ nu siawo le Greenland. Le duawo me hã la, "nutome sesẽ " aɖekewo meli o.
text_en: Crime, and ill-will toward foreigners in general, is virtually unknown in Greenland. Even in the towns, there are no "rough areas."

text: Yame ƒe vuvɔwɔwɔ koe nye kuxi sesẽ nyanyɛ si me ame si medzra ɖo hafi va o la ato.
text_en: Cold weather is perhaps the only real danger the unprepared will face.

text: Nenye be nèɖi tsa yi ɖe Greenland le vuvɔŋɔli la (nya be nenye be nèle dziehe kpa dzi yim la, nenemakee vuvɔ la aganɔ sesẽm ɖe edzi), ele vevie be nàtsɔ awu siwo me dzoxɔxɔ aɖe le, siwo asu wò nyuie la vɛ.
text_en: If you visit Greenland during cold seasons (considering that the further north you go, the colder it will be), it is essential to bring warm enough clothing.

text: Ale si ŋkeke siwo le dzomeŋɔli me didii la ate ŋu ana be alɔ̃ maɖi na amewo nyuie o eye agate ŋu ahe lãmesẽ menɔnɔkuxi bubu siwo ku ɖe eŋu la vɛ
text_en: The very long days in the summer can lead to problems getting sufficient sleep and associated health issues.

text: Le dzomeŋɔli la, gànɔ ŋudzɔ le Dukɔa me ƒe muwo ŋu. Togbɔ be womedea dɔ lãme na ame o la, ate ŋu aɖe fu ŋutɔ.
text_en: During the summer, also watch out for the Nordic mosquitoes. Although they do not transmit any diseases, they can be irritating.

text: Đe ale si Sn Francisco ƒe ganyawo le ta, wotsͻ nɛ sͻna kple modzakatsaɖiƒe gãtͻ siwo le xexeame, eƒe ganyawo yia dzi ale gbegbe.
text_en: While San Francisco's economy is linked to it being a world-class tourist attraction, its economy is diversified.

text: Akpa siwo dͻwͻɖuia bͻ ɖo wue nye dziɖuɖudͻwͻƒewo, ganyadzikpͻdͻwͻƒe, asitsatsa kple modzakatsaɖiƒewo.
text_en: The largest employment sectors are professional services, government, finance, trade, and tourism.

text: Ezazã atraɖie le hagbewo, nͻnͻmetatawo, agbeŋutinyawo kple dekͻnu nyanyeewo kpe ɖe dukͻa kple enͻƒe ŋu be woƒe ŋkͻ nyͻ le xexeame godoo.
text_en: Its frequent portrayal in music, films, literature and popular culture has helped make the city and its landmarks known throughout the world.

text: San Fracisco tu modzakatsaɖiƒe gã aɖe si yͻ fŭu kle amedzrodzeƒewo, nuɖuƒewo kple azãɖuƒe gãwo.
text_en: San Francisco has developed a large tourist infrastructure with numerous hotels, restaurants, and top-notch convention facilities.

text: San Francisco nye teƒe nyui kekeakewo dometͻ ɖeka le dukͻa me na Asiatͻwo, Koreatͻwo, Thitͻwo, Indiantͻwo kple Japanisiawo.
text_en: San Francisco is also one of the best places in the nation for other Asian cuisine: Korean, Thai, Indian, and Japanese.

text: Mͻzͻzͻ de Walt Disney ƒe xexeme ɖe ko le abe Amerikatͻwo ƒe mͻ legbe zͻzͻ de subͻsubͻƒe ene.
text_en: Traveling to Walt Disney World represents a major pilgrimage for many American families.

text: Kpͻɖeŋu vevi ɖekae nye yameטuɖoɖo alo טuɖoɖo yi ɖe amedzrodzeƒe si le Disney, anͻ teƒe ma abe kͻsiɖa ɖeka ene hafi atrͻ yi aƒeme.
text_en: The "typical" visit involves flying into Orlando International Airport, busing to an on-site Disney hotel, spending about a week without leaving Disney property, and returning home.

text: Seɖoƒe aɖeke meli nɛ o, nu sia ŋu koe amewo wͻ nɛ ne wole nu ƒom tso Disney dede ŋu.
text_en: There are infinite variations possible, but this remains what most people mean when they talk of "going to Disney World".

text: Tiketi geɖe siwo wozãna le yaטãla dzi la, nye esi wozã kpͻ.
text_en: Many tickets sold online through auction websites such as eBay or Craigslist are partially used multi-day park-hopper tickets.

text: Esime nu sia yia edze gbawo tsyo gbe la, Disney ya ɖo asi dzi; ame bbu aɖe ke mate vu azã tiketi ma ke o.
text_en: While this is a very common activity, it is prohibited by Disney: the tickets are non-transferable.

text: Ƒuƒoƒo ɖe sia ɖe le Grand Canyon ƒe toa gɔme hiã mɔɖeɖe gbale xɔxɔ
text_en: Any camping below the rim in Grand Canyon requires a backcountry permit.

text: Mɔɖeɖegbalẽ ʋɛ aɖewo koe wona be woana balia nanɔ dedienɔnɔ me, ahanɔ anyi le dzinua ƒe ŋkeke gbãtɔ dzi, dzinu ene do ŋgɔ na dzinu si woadze egɔme la.
text_en: Permits are limited to protect the canyon, and become available on the 1st day of the month, four months prior to the start month.

text: Eya ta, mɔɖegbalẽ xɔxɔ ɖe sia ɖe le Dame me la adze gɔme tso Dzove 1 dzi.
text_en: Thus, a backcountry permit for any start date in May becomes available on 1 Jan.

text: Teƒe le afi siwo ame geɖe nya, abe Bright Angel Campground le Phantom Ranch lɔƒo, si yɔna fũu kple biabia xɔxɔ tso ŋkeke gbãtɔ si dzi woʋu enu la hena elelé daɖi.
text_en: Space for the most popular areas, such as the Bright Angel Campground adjacent to Phantom Ranch, generally fill up by the requests received on first date they are opened to reservations.

text: Mɔɖeɖegbalẽ xexleme ʋee aɖewo koe li na numekuku biabiawo le ame si va gbãtɔ gbɔe woakpɔ gbã ƒe ɖoɖonu.
text_en: There are a limited number permits reserved for walk-in requests available on a first come, first served basis.

text: Gege ɖe Afrika ƒe ɣetoɖoƒe kple טu nye mͻ nyui aɖe si dzi nato ahakpͻ eƒe atsyͻdzedze agade modzakatsaɖiƒe siwo mate ŋu ade טu manͻ mee.
text_en: Entering Southern Africa by car is an amazing way to see all the region's beauty as well as to get to places off the normal tourist routes.

text: Nu sia ate ŋu ayi dzi le טu ŋutͻwo me le ɖoɖo nyuiwo wͻwͻ me gake 4x4 zazã nyo awu eye teƒe geɖewo la, 4x4 koe ate ŋu ade.
text_en: This can be done in a normal car with careful planning but a 4x4 is highly advised and many locations are only accessible with a high wheel base 4x4.

text: Ne ele wo ɖoɖowo wͻm la, nenͻ wo susu me be, togbͻ be Afrika ƒe ɣetoɖoƒe dze mo anyi hã, menye du bubu siwo ƒo xlae la katãe o.
text_en: Keep in mind while planning that although Southern Africa is stable not all neighboring countries are.

text: Nu siwo hiã na wo mͻzͻgbalĕvi wͻwͻ ka dukͻ si me netso.
text_en: Visa requirements and costs vary from nation to nation and are affected by the country you come from.

text: Dukͻ ɖe sia ɖe ƒe se kple ɖoɖowo to vovo tso wo nͻewo gbͻ ku ɖe nu siwo ahiã vevie le טua me.
text_en: Each country also has unique laws requiring what emergency items need to be in the car.

text: Victoria tsisisi nye du aɖe si le Zimbabwe adziehe kpa dzi, tso Livingstone border gbͻ, Zambia hete ɖe Botswana ŋu.
text_en: Victoria Falls is a town in the western portion of Zimbabwe, across the border from Livingstone, Zambia, and near Botswana.

text: Dua te ɖe tsi ŋu tututu, eye wonye teƒe vevi si amewo dina be yewoade, gake modzakatsaɖiƒe sia nana mͻnukpͻkpͻ ame siwo katã va na afi ma la be woate ŋu anͻ anyi didi.
text_en: The town lies immediately next to the falls, and they are the major attraction, but this popular tourist destination offers both adventure seekers and sightseers plenty of opportunities for a longer stay.

text: Le tsidzaŋͻli (Ademekpͻxɛ va de asi na Tadoxɛ), etsi ƒe kpekpeme yina dzi eye tsisisiwo hã nͻ agbo dzem.
text_en: In the rainy season (November to March), the water volume will be higher and the Falls will be more dramatic.

text: Aƒo tsi bele ne etso bridzia alo nezͻ le mͻ si te ɖe tsisisia ŋu.
text_en: You are guaranteed to get wet if you cross the bridge or walk along the trails winding near the Falls.

text: Le go bubu me hã, eyia dzi nenema elabena tsia ƒe kpekpeme yi dzi ale gbegbe be hafi nade dzesi tsisisia ŋutͻ la, tsiawo katã aɖe fu na wo.
text_en: On the other hand, it is precisely because the volume of water is so high that your viewing of the actual Falls will be obscured—by all the water!

text: Tutankhamun ƒe yͻdo (KV62). KV62 anye yͻdo xͻ ŋkͻ kekeake le balia me, Howard Carter ƒe nukpͻkpͻ le ƒe 1922 me ɖe fia vi ɖiɖi ƒe nuwͻnawo do goe.
text_en: Tomb of Tutankhamun (KV62). KV62 may be the most famous of the tombs in the Valley, the scene of Howard Carter's 1922 discovery of the almost intact royal burial of the young king.

text: Tsͻ sͻ kple yͻdo bubuawo la, Tutankhamun ƒe yͻdo gbͻe amewo mete ŋu de na o, ele sue eye womeɖo atsyͻ hã nɛ fŭ o.
text_en: Compared to most of the other royal tombs, however, the tomb of Tutankhamun is barely worth visiting, being much smaller and with limited decoration.

text: Ame sia ame si me didi ma anͻ be yeakpͻ nu si gblĕ le esime wole agbagba dzem be yewoaɖee ɖa le aɖaka me la, awͻ ŋku na wo be eƒe abͻta kple ta koe le dzedzeƒe.
text_en: Anyone interested in seeing evidence of the damage to the mummy done during attempts to remove it from the coffin will be disappointed as only the head and shoulders are visible.

text: Kpe xͻ asi wͻ nukuwo megale eme o gake woɖe wo ɖa kͻ yi Egypte ƒe nͻnͻmetatawo kple atikpakpawo nͻ ƒe.
text_en: The fabulous riches of the tomb are no longer in it, but have been removed to the Egyptian Museum in Cairo.

text: Mͻzͻla siwo si ɣeyiɣi sͻ agbͻ aɖeke mele o la adi be yewoagble yewoƒe game ɖe teƒe bubu.
text_en: Visitors with limited time would be best to spend their time elsewhere.

text: Phnom Krom, agbadroƒe 12 le Siem Reap ƒe ɣetoɖoƒe le ƒe alafa asieke 9th mawo me, Wotu to gbedoxͻ sia le Fia Yasovarman ƒe dziɖuɣi.
text_en: Phnom Krom, 12 km southwest of Siem Reap. This hilltop temple was built at the end of the 9th century, during the reign of King Yasovarman.

text: Ale si teƒa fã kple Tonle Sap tͻ ƒe dzedzeme na be toa lialia dze.
text_en: The gloomy atmosphere of the temple and the view over the Tonle Sap lake make the climb to the hill worthwhile.

text: Teƒe aɖe sasrã kpͻ ate ŋu anͻ bͻbͻe to tͻdziטuwo zazã me kͻ yi tͻ gã gbͻe.
text_en: A visit to the site can be conveniently combined with a boat trip to the lake.

text: Angkor gbaĕvi hiã be natsͻ age ɖe gbedoxͻ me eya ta wͻ ɖe edzi megaŋlͻ agbalĕvia be ne edze mͻ yina ɖe Tonle Sap tͻ to o.
text_en: The Angkor Pass is needed to enter the temple so do not forget to bring your passport along when heading to Tonle Sap.

text: Jerusalem nye toxͻ du kple du gãtͻ na Israel, togbͻ be dukͻ geɖewo medea dzesie be enye Israel ƒe toxͻ du o.
text_en: Jerusalem is the capital and largest city of Israel, though most other countries and the United Nations do not recognize it as Israel's capital.

text: ŋutinya vivi si li ƒe akpewo sͻe ya ƒo nu tsotsã du xoxo si le Juda Towo me.
text_en: The ancient city in the Judean Hills has a fascinating history spanning thousands of years.

text: Dya ŋuti kͻ na subͻsubͻ hawo kple dekͻnu nuwo wͻƒe.
text_en: The city is holy to the three monotheistic religions - Judaism, Christianity and Islam, and serves as a spiritual, religious, and cultural center.

text: Đe ale si dua le vevie na subͻsubͻhawo ta la, Jerusale nye teƒe si amewo ɖina tsa dena le Israel.
text_en: Due to the religious significance of the city, and in particular the many sites of the Old City area, Jerusalem is one of the main tourist destinations in Israel.

text: Tsã nuleɖiwo, amegbetͻŋutinuwosrͻƒe kple dekͻnu teƒewo, hekpe ɖe nuƒleƒewo kple nuɖuƒewo le Jerusalem.
text_en: Jerusalem has many historic, archeological and cultural sites, along with vibrant and crowded shopping centers, cafés, and restaurants.

text: Equador dukͻa bia tso Cubatͻwo si be woaxͻ kpekpegbalĕ do ŋgͻ na gege ɖe Equador kͻ yi yameטuɖoƒewo.
text_en: Ecuador requires that Cuban citizens receive an invitation letter prior to entering Ecuador through international airports or frontier admission points.

text: Edz be Ecuadorian dudͻwͻha si kpͻa gbetanyawo gbͻ la nade asi agbalĕa te be woanͻ se te eye nuhiãhiã aɖewo hã nakpe ɖe eŋu.
text_en: This letter must be legalized by the Ecuadorian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and comply with certain requirements.

text: Wotrͻ asi le nuhiãhiã mawo ŋu da ɖi be woakpͻ egbͻ be amewo ƒe mͻzͻnyawo yi dukͻ eve siawo dome nanͻ ɖoɖo tͻxɛ blibo me.
text_en: These requirements are designed to provide an organized migratory flow between both countries.

text: Cubatͻ siwo si Amerika gbemumudukͻmegbalĕ la le la, edze be woakpͻ Euador dziɖuɖuteƒe la ne woaɖe wo tso agbalĕ hiãhiã mawo ƒe ga me.
text_en: Cuban citizens who are US green card holders should visit an Ecuadorian Consulate to obtain an exemption to this requirement.

text: Ele be gbe si gbe wò mɔzɔgbãlevi aku la nanye ɣleti ade si kplɔ wò yiyi kple gbɔgbɔ ŋkekewo ɖo teti. Yiyi kple gbɔgbɔ ƒe tikiti/tikiti si fia be ame xe fe ɖe mɔzɔzɔ ta la hiã hena ɣeyiɣi si sinu ànɔ anyi la ɖeɖefia.
text_en: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond your travel dates. A round/onward trip ticket is needed to prove the length of your stay.

text: Tsaɖiɖi ƒe fe dzi ka ɖiɖina na ame siwo le habɔbɔ gãwo me, eya ta nenye be wò ɖeka alo wò kple xɔ̃ wò aɖe koe le yiyim la, dze agbagba nàdi ame bubuwo eye mianɔ ene va se ɖe ade ale be mi kata miaxe tsaɖila ɖeka ƒe fe; esia nyo wu be ame ɖeka ko naxee.
text_en: Tours are cheaper for larger groups, so if you're by yourself or with just one friend, try to meet other people and form a group of four to six for a better per-person rate.

text: Ke mele be wò susu neɖe ɖa le eŋu o, elabena zi geɖe la, woblena tsaɖilawo be woage ɖe ʋuawo me.
text_en: However, this shouldn't really be off your concern, because often tourists are shuffled around to fill the cars.

text: Le nyateƒe me la, enye mɔnu si dzi wotona heblena amewo ale be woabu be ele be yewoagaxe ga ɖe edzi
text_en: It seems actually to be more a way of tricking people into believing they have to pay more.

text: Machu Picchu ƒe anyiehe nuwuƒe 'kpa dzie to kɔkɔ sia, si dzena le foto siwo fia ale si wòkakae la le.
text_en: Towering above the north end of Machu Picchu is this steep mountain, often the backdrop to many photos of the ruins.

text: Edze abe nu sesẽ ene nenye be nèle anyime, ekɔkɔ eye elialia sesẽ, ke ame sesẽ kakowo ya la woate ŋu alia etame le abe miniti 45 me ene.
text_en: It looks a bit daunting from below, and it is a steep and difficult ascent, but most reasonably fit persons should be able to make it in about 45 minutes.

text: Woɖo kpe trakpuiwo ɖe mɔawo ƒe akpa geɖe dzi, eye anyigbateƒe siwo kɔ yi dzime la, woɖo gayibɔ sesẽwo ɖi ale be woanye atrakpuiŋusilēƒewo.
text_en: Stone steps are laid along most of the path, and in the steeper sections steel cables provide a supporting handrail.

text: Eya ta nɔ mɔkpɔm be gbɔgbɔ tsixe natsi wò ƒo, eye nàlé ŋku ɖe ɖokuiwò ŋu nyuie le teƒe siwo gaɖiabu wu, vevietɔ nenye be ba le anyigba la, elabe ate ŋu anye nu si ahe afɔku geɖe vɛ le ɣeyiɣi kpui aɖe me
text_en: That said, expect to be out of breath, and take care in the steeper portions, especially when wet, as it can become dangerous quickly.

text: Agado vi sue aɖe le etame si me wòle be woato, etame mekɔkɔ o, eye ele be nàbɔbɔ ta alegbegbe.
text_en: There's a tiny cave near the top that must be passed through, it is quite low and a rather tight squeeze.

text: Nenye be nèdi be yeakpɔ Galapagos ƒe blema nuwɔɖiwo kple dzɔdzɔme nuwɔwɔ siwo mebɔ ɖe ame dome o la, mɔ nyuietɔe nye be nàzã tɔdziʋu sue, abe ale si Charles Darwin wɔ le ƒe 1835 me ene.
text_en: Seeing the sites and wildlife of the Galapagos is best done by boat, just as Charles Darwin did it in 1835.

text: Tɔdziʋu siwo tsɔa amewo, siwo zɔna Galapagos tsiwo dzi la le 60 kple edzi vɔ, - wotsɔa mɔzɔla 8 va se ɖe 100.
text_en: Over 60 cruise ships ply the Galapagos waters - ranging in size from 8 to 100 passengers.

text: Ame geɖewo xea fe heléa nɔƒe ɖi do ŋgɔ na mɔzɔzɔ la (elabena nenye be ɣeyiɣi si me wozɔa mɔ koŋ ɖo la, tɔdzuʋu sue la yɔna zi geɖe).
text_en: Most people book their place well in advance (as the boats are usually full during the high season).

text: Kpɔ egbɔ be ame si dzi nèto helé nɔƒea ɖi la nya nu nyuie tso Galapagos ŋuti eye eganya nu tso tɔdziʋu vovovowo ŋu.
text_en: Be sure the agent through whom you book is a Galapagos specialist with a good knowledge of a wide variety of ships.

text: Esia ana be woatsɔ wò ada ɖe tɔdziʋu nyuitɔ me, eye esia asɔ ɖe nu siwo nèdi kple/alo nu siwo mèdi o la nu.
text_en: This will ensure that your particular interests and/or constraints are matched with the ship most suitable to them.

text: Do ŋgɔ na Spaintɔwo ƒe vava le ƒe alafa 16 lia me la, anyiehe Chile tɔwo nɔ Inca tɔwo ƒe kpɔkplɔ te le esime Araucaniatɔwo (Mapuche) ŋutɔ nɔ Chile ƒe titina kple anyiehe nutowo me.
text_en: Before the Spanish arrived in the 16th century, northern Chile was under Inca rule while the indigenous Araucanians (Mapuche) inhabited central and southern Chile.

text: Mapuchetɔwo hã ganɔ blema Amerikatɔwo ƒe hatsotso mamlɛ, siwo kpɔ ɖokuisinɔnɔ, siwo menɔ ame siwo do Spaingbe ƒe kpɔkplɔ te tututu va se ɖe Chile ƒe ɖokuisinɔnɔ megbe o la dome.
text_en: The Mapuche were also one of the last independent American indigenous groups, that were not fully absorbed into Spanish-speaking rule until after Chile's independence.

text: Togbɔ be Chile ɖe gbeƒã be yexɔ ɖokuisinɔnɔ le ƒe 1810 me (le Napoleon-ʋa siwo na be dziɖuɖu ŋusẽgã menɔ Spain si le ƒe aɖewo me o) la, womekpɔ dziɖuɖu blibo ɖe Spaintɔwo dzi tututu o va se ɖe ƒe 1818 me.
text_en: Although Chile declared independence in 1810 (amid the Napoleonic wars that left Spain without a functioning central government for a couple of years), decisive victory over the Spanish was not achieved until 1818.

text: Dominican Republic (Spainish: Republica Dominicana) la nye Caribbean dukɔ si xɔ ɣedzeƒe lɔƒo ƒe afã na Hispaniola ƒukpo la, si wòma kple Haiti
text_en: The Dominican Republic (Spanish: República Dominicana) is a Caribbean country that occupies the eastern half of the island of Hispaniola, which it shares with Haiti

text: To vovo na keƒuta ɣiwo kple tonyigbãwo la, dukɔ la nye teƒe ne Europatɔwo du xoxotɔ kekeake le Amerikas si va zu Santo Domingo ƒe akpa aɖe
text_en: Besides white sand beaches and mountain landscapes, the country is home to the oldest European city in the Americas, now part of Santo Domingo.

text: Tainotɔwo kple Caribtɔwoe nye ame gbãtɔ siwo nɔ ƒukpo la dzi. Caribtɔwo la, wonye Arawakangbe dola siwo va ɖo le ƒe 10,000 D.M.Ŋ lɔƒo
text_en: The island was first inhabited by the Taínos and Caribes. The Caribes were an Arawakan-speaking people who had arrived around 10,000 BCE.

text: Le ƒe ʋɛ aɖewo si kplɔ Yuropa mɔzɔlawo ƒe vava la ɖo la, Spain aʋdziɖulawo ɖe Tainotɔwo ƒe agbɔsɔsɔ dzi kpɔtɔ ŋutɔ
text_en: Within a few short years following the arrival of European explorers, the population of Tainos had significantly been reduced by the Spanish conquerors

text: Le Fray Bartolomé de las Casas (Tratado de las Indias) ƒe nya nu, le ƒe 1492 kple 1498 dome la, Spain aʋadziɖulawo wu Taintɔwo abe ame 100,000 ene.
text_en: Based on Fray Bartolomé de las Casas (Tratado de las Indias) between 1492 and 1498 the Spanish conquerors killed around 100,000 Taínos.

text: Jardin de la Unión. Wotu teƒe sia be wòanye kpekpeƒe na saɖeagaxɔ aɖe si nɔ anyi le ƒe alafa 17 lia me, eye Templo de San Diego koe ganye xɔ si tsi anyi.
text_en: Jardín de la Unión. This space was built as the atrium for a 17th-century convent, of which the Templo de San Diego is the sole surviving building.

text: Azɔ la eva zu takpeƒe koŋ, eye nu geɖewo yina edzi le afi ma ɣesiaɣi, zã kple keli.
text_en: It now functions as the central plaza, and always has a lot of things going on, day and night.

text: Nuɖuƒe geɖewo ƒoxlã abɔ la me, eye wowɔa modzakaɖewɔna siwo womexɔa ga ɖe wo ta o zi geɖe tso gazebo ƒe titina me.
text_en: There are a number of restaurants surrounding the garden, and in the afternoons and evening there free concerts are often given from the central gazebo.

text: Callejon del Beso (Kpɔdome si Wogbugbɔ nu le). Akpata eve siwo ƒe dometsotso ko nye centimeta 69 nye lɔlɔ̃tɔ wɔnuteƒe aɖe ƒe aƒe me.
text_en: Callejon del Beso (Alley of the Kiss). Two balconies separated by only 69 centimeters is home of an old love legend.

text: Ɖevi aɖewo woagblɔ ŋutinya la na wò nenye be nètsɔ peni sue aɖewo na wò.
text_en: For a few pennies some children will tell you the story.

text: Bowen Ƒukpo nye teƒe nyanyɛ aɖe si amewo ɖia tsa yina ŋkeke ɖeka sɔŋ alo le kɔsiɖa ƒe nuwuwu. Woate ŋu awɔ tɔdziʋusue ƒe hoʋiʋli si wowɔna le tsi dzi, agalia to le afi ma. Fiasewo, nuɖuƒewo kpakple nu bubu geɖewo hã le afi ma.
text_en: Bowen Island is a popular day trip or weekend excursion offering kayaking, hiking, shops, restaurants, and more.

text: Nutoa me ŋutɔ le Howe Sound le Vancouver-mɔ dzi eye woate ŋu aɖo afi ma bɔbɔe to tɔdziʋu siwo tsɔ amewo tso Grandville Fukpo dzi le Vancouver dua godo
text_en: This authentic community is located in Howe Sound just off Vancouver, and is easily accessed via scheduled water taxis departing Granville Island in downtown Vancouver.

text: Nenye be nènye ame si lɔ̃na gota fefewo wɔwɔ la, ekema mɔzɔzɔ le Atsiaƒu ƒe yame yi ɖe Sky Corridor le vevie.
text_en: For those who enjoy outdoor activities, a trek up the Sea to Sky corridor is essential.

text: Whistler (gaƒoƒo ɖeka kple afã ƒe ʋukuku tso Vancouver) xɔ asi ke amewo nyae ɖe ƒe 2010 Vuvɔŋɔli Olympik wɔnawo ta.
text_en: Whistler (1.5 hour drive from Vancouver) is expensive but well-known because of the 2010 Winter Olympics.

text: Le vuvɔŋɔli la, kpɔ gome le sno dzi zɔzɔ fefe wɔna nyuitɔ kekeake aɖewo me le Amerika ƒe Dziehe kpa dzi me, eye le dzomeŋɔli me la, dze agbagba nàdo gasɔ le to dzi le mɔ nyuitɔ dzi.
text_en: In the winter, enjoy some of the best skiing in North America, and in the summer try some authentic mountain biking.

text: Ele be nàbia mɔ do ŋgɔ. Ele be nàbia mɔ be yeatsi Sirena amlɔ
text_en: Permits must be reserved in advance. You must have a permit to stay overnight at Sirena.

text: Sirena koe nye Modzakatsaɖidɔwɔƒe ɖeka toŋ, si naa anyimlɔƒe kple nuɖoɖo dzodzoewo kpe ɖe asaɖawɔwɔ ŋu koe le La Leona, San Pedrillo kpakple Los Patos, ke womeɖaa nu dzra o.
text_en: Sirena is the only ranger station that offers dormitory lodging and hot meals in addition to camping. La Leona, San Pedrillo, and Los Patos offer only camping with no food service.

text: Ele bɔbɔe be nàxɔ abɔ la ƒe mɔɖeɖewo tso Modzakatsaɖidɔwɔƒe si le Puerto Jiménez, ke womexɔna agbananuƒlegbalẽviwo o.
text_en: It is possible to secure park permits directly from the Ranger Station in Puerto Jiménez, but they do not accept credit cards

text: Ablɔ Dɔwɔƒea (MINAE) menaa ablɔ mɔɖeɖewo wòwua ɣleti ɖeka do ŋgɔ na tsaɖila la ƒe vava o.
text_en: The Park Service (MINAE) does not issue park permits more than one month in advance of anticipated arrival.

text: CafeNet El Sol léa teƒe ɖe anyi na amewo. Woxɔna $30, alo $10 nenye be amea atsi anyi ŋkeke ɖeka; numekɔkɔ geɖe ku ɖe esia ŋu le woƒe Corcovado internat-nuŋlɔƒe dzi.
text_en: CafeNet El Sol offers a reservation service for a fee of US$30, or $10 for one-day passes; details on their Corcovado page.

text: Cook Fukpowo nye ƒukpo-dukɔ aɖe si le ɖekawɔwɔ me kple New Zealand, le Polynesia, le Anyiehe- Pasifik 'Tsiaƒu la ƒe titina.
text_en: The Cook Islands are an island country in free association with New Zealand, located in Polynesia, in the middle of the South Pacific Ocean.

text: Enye ƒukpo ƒokpli si me ƒukpo 15 siwo kaka ɖe atsiaƒu si nye kilometa togodo miliɔn 2.2 la ŋu.
text_en: It is an archipelago with 15 islands spread out over 2.2 million km2 of ocean.

text: Ƒukpoa ƒe ɣeyiɣi sɔ kple Hawai ƒe ɣeyiɣi, eye ɣeaɖewo ɣi la, amewo kpɔa ƒukpoawo be wonye "Hawaii anyigbe gɔme."
text_en: With the same time zone as Hawaii, the islands are sometimes thought of as "Hawaii down under".

text: Togbɔ be ele sue wu Hawai hã la, enaa be modzakatsaɖila tsitsiwo ɖoa ŋku ale si Hawai nɔ hafi wòvazu dukɔnɔɖokuisi si, ale si wònɔ esime modzakatsaɖilawo ƒe dzeƒe gãwo kple nu bubuwo menɔ anyi o.
text_en: Though smaller, it reminds some elderly visitors of Hawaii before statehood without all the large tourist hotels and other development.

text: Du gãwo mele Cook Ƒukpoawo me o, ke boŋ ƒukpo 15 vovovoe le eme. Nyanyɛtɔwo koŋue nye Rarotonga kple Aitutaki.
text_en: The Cook Islands do not have any cities but are composed of 15 different islands. The main ones are Rarotonga and Aitutaki.

text: Le dukɔ deŋgɔwo me egbe la, aba nyui bɔbɔe xɔasiwo kple ŋdi nuɖuɖuwo nana vazu atsyia nu.
text_en: In developed countries today, providing deluxe bed and breakfasts has been raised to a sort of art-form.

text: Le dzime nuwuwu la, edze kɔtɛe be amedzrodzeƒewo tea kame kuɖe nu eve ŋu: abaɖoɖo kple ŋdi nuɖuɖu ŋu.
text_en: At the top end, B&Bs obviously compete mainly on two main things: bedding and breakfast.

text: Eya ta nenye be nèɖo amedzrodzeƒe nyuitɔ kekeake la, àdi aba nyui bɔbɔe xɔasitɔ wu, ɖewomahĩ anye aba si wolɔ̃na kple asi alo blema 'ba tɔgbui aɖe.
text_en: Accordingly, at the finest such establishments one is apt to find the most luxurious bedding, maybe a handmade quilt or an antique bed.

text: Ŋdi nuɖuɖuwo ate ŋu alɔ nutoa me ƒe nuɖuɖu tɔxɛwo alo ame si gbɔ wodze la ƒe nuɖuɖu vevie ɖe eme.
text_en: Breakfast may include seasonal delights of the region or the host's speciality dish.

text: Woate ŋu aɖo kplɔ̃a ɖe blema xɔ xoxo aɖe, si ƒe kplɔ̃ kple zikpuiwo kple atikpakpa bubuwo nye blema nuwo, anyigba si woɖo atsyɔ̃ na kplakple tsiƒuƒe.
text_en: The setting might be an historic old building with antique furnishings, manicured grounds and a swimming pool.

text: Gege ɖe wò ŋutɔ wò ʋu me kple ʋukuku le mɔdodo didi aɖe dzi la hena dzidzeme aɖe vɛ, kploe ɖe ko.
text_en: Getting into your own car and heading off on a long road trip has an intrinsic appeal in its simplicity.

text: Mele abe ʋu gãwo o; elabe ɖewomahĩ wò ŋutɔ wò ʋukuku ma wò eye nènya eƒe mɔxenuwo.
text_en: Unlike larger vehicles, you are probably already familiar with driving your car and know its limitations.

text: Agbadɔ wɔwɔ ɖe ame aɖe ƒe anyigba dzi alo le du ɖe sia ɖe ƒomevi me, meka eƒe lolome o, ate ŋu ahe amewo ƒe susu va dzi wò le mɔnu si mèdi la nu o.
text_en: Setting up a tent on private property or in a town of any size can easily attract unwanted attention.

text: Kploe ko la, wò ʋu nye mɔ nyuie aɖe si dzi nàto azɔ mɔ, ke ezazã "ayi asaɖawɔƒe" mebɔ o.
text_en: In short, using your car is a great way to take a road trip but seldom in itself a way to "camp".

text: Asaɖawɔƒe yiyi kple ʋu le bɔbɔe nenye be minivan, SUV, Sedan alo Station Wagon gã, siwo ƒe zikpuiwo ate ŋu amlɔ anyi la le asi wò.
text_en: Car camping is possible if you have a large minivan, SUV, Sedan or Station Wagon with seats that lay down.

text: Amedzrodzeƒe aɖewo li tso dzudzɔ ketekewo kple tɔdziʋu siwo tsɔa agba gãwo ƒe ŋɔli ke; do ŋgɔ na Xexeme Ʋa Evelia, le ƒe alafa 19 lia alo 20 wo ƒe gɔmedzedze.
text_en: Some hotels have a heritage from the golden age of steam railways and ocean liners; before the Second World War, in the 19th or early 20th centuries.

text: Amedzrodzeƒe siawoe hotsuitɔ kple ameŋkutawo nɔna, eye zi geɖe la, woɖu nu nyuie hemlɔ anyi nyuie.
text_en: These hotels were where the rich and the famous of the day would stay, and often had fine dining and nightlife.

text: Xɔmenu xoxowo woe le wo si. Ŋkuʋuʋui nuwo hã mele wo si o, eye woƒe nuwo do xoxo alegbegbe.
text_en: The old fashioned fittings, the lack of the latest amenities, and a certain graceful agedness are also part of their character.

text: Togbɔ be zi geɖe la, wonyena ame aɖe tɔ la, dukɔkplɔla tso dukɔ bubuwo me kple ame ŋkuta bubu, siwo ɖi tsa va la dzena wo me.
text_en: While they are usually privately owned, they sometimes accommodate visiting heads of state and other dignitaries.

text: Mɔzɔla si si ga bɔ ɖa la ate ŋu aɖoe le tame be yeatsa le xexea me godoo, agavadze amedzrodzeƒe siawo tɔgbui geɖe.
text_en: A traveller with piles of money might consider a round the world flight, broken up with stays in many of these hotels.

text: Amedzroxɔxɔ tso teƒe ɖeka yi teƒe bubu ƒe katiatiahabɔbɔ nye dɔwɔƒe si naa be katiatia nɔna mɔzɔlawo kple du gã siwo woaɖi tsa ayi la me tɔwo dome.
text_en: A hospitality exchange network is the organization that connects travelers with locals in the cities they are going to visit.

text: Zi geɖe la, katiatia habɔbɔ sia ƒomevi me nɔnɔ hiã na intanet-dzi "gbãlevi aɖe ƒe ɖoɖowo ŋu ɖoɖo; togbɔ be katiatia habɔbɔ aɖewo gadina be ame nagatsɔ nu bubu siwo ku ɖe amea ŋu la akpe ɖe eŋu hã.
text_en: Joining such a network usually just requires filling out an online form; although some networks offer or require additional verification.

text: Woayi edzi aŋlɔ amedzrodzeƒewo ƒe ŋkɔ ɖe agbalẽ dzi alo adae ɖe intanet dzi, eye ɣeaɖewo ɣi la, wotsɔa mɔzɔla bubuwo ƒe ɖaseɖiɖiwo ku ɖe amedzrodzeƒe siawo ŋu kpena ɖe eŋu.
text_en: A listing of available hosts is then provided either in print and/or online, sometimes with references and reviews by other travelers.

text: Woɖo Couchsurfing anyi le Dzove me, le 2004 me esime kɔmpiutaŋutidɔwɔla, Caset Fenton kpɔ yameʋu aɖe si yina ɖe Iceland le asi bɔbɔe dzi ke mekpɔ dzeƒe o.
text_en: Couchsurfing was founded in January 2004 after computer programmer Casey Fenton found a cheap flight to Iceland but did not have a place to stay.

text: Eɖo email ɖe sukuvi siwo nɔ dukɔa ƒe sukukɔkɔ me eye wo dometɔ geɖewo doe ɖa be yewoanae dzeƒe femaxee.
text_en: He emailed students at the local university and received an overwhelming number of offers for free accommodation.

text: Sɔhewo-amedzro si xɔ ƒe blaeve va se ɖe ƒe blaeve vɔ asieke-koŋue nɔa amedzrodzeƒe siwo wozãa tsilekpɔ kple nuɖaƒe ɖeka le, ke àte ŋu akpɔ mɔzɔla siwo tsi wu wo hã le wo me.
text_en: Hostels cater primarily to young people – a typical guest is in their twenties – but you can often find older travellers there too.

text: Asesẽ hafi àkpɔ ƒome aɖe si va kple ɖeviwo, ke amedzrodzeƒe siwo wozãa tsilekpɔ kple nuɖaƒe ɖeka le dometɔ aɖewo lɔ̃na be woanɔ xɔ siwo me ame aɖeke manɔ kpe ɖe woŋu o la me.
text_en: Families with children are a rare sight, but some hostels do allow them in private rooms.

text: Beijing-du gã si le Chinae mee woawɔ Vuvɔme Olimpik Fefewo le, le ƒe 2022 me, si ana be wòanye du gã gbatɔ si me wowɔ Olimpik fefewo le, le dzomeŋɔli kple vuvɔŋɔli sia.
